title: Relative free cocompletion with prescribed cocones and finite-variable universal property
statement:
Use the universes and infinity categories of [def-coef-complete-algebroid] and the coherent diagrams, cocones and functor categories of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]; small always means in the fixed universe $\mathcal U$. Let $C$ be an infinity category and $R$ a collection of specified coherent cocones $r_\alpha$, each consisting of a diagram $F_\alpha:K_\alpha\to C$, an apex $x_\alpha\in C$ and a coherent transformation $F_\alpha\to\Delta_{K_\alpha}x_\alpha$, where $K_\alpha$ is a small simplicial set and $\Delta_{K_\alpha}$ denotes the constant-diagram functor. Empty bases are allowed. These cocones need not be colimiting in $C$. After enlarging the ambient universe to contain the data, there exist a cocomplete infinity category $P_R(C)$ and $j_R:C\to P_R(C)$ sending every member of $R$ to a colimiting cocone. For every infinity category $Z$ admitting all small colimits, restriction is an equivalence
$$\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{colim}}(P_R(C),Z)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_R(C,Z),$$
where the right side is the full coherent functor category on functors sending the specified cocones to colimiting cocones, and the left side is the full category on functors preserving small colimits. All these equivalences include natural transformations and higher simplices.

For every finite list $(C_i,R_i)$, restriction along $\prod_i j_{R_i}$ likewise gives an equivalence from the full category of functors $\prod_iP_{R_i}(C_i)\to Z$ preserving small colimits separately to the full category of functors $\prod_iC_i\to Z$ sending each $R_i$ to colimiting cocones when the other variables are fixed. This includes the empty list (both functor categories are $Z$). These restriction equivalences are natural in $Z$ and compatible with restriction to any variables; their full faithfulness identifies spaces of coherent transformations, equivalences and all their compatibility homotopies.

If $C$ and the collection $R$ are small, $P_R(C)$ is presentable, in the meaning of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], relative to $\mathcal U$. More precisely, let $y:C\to\mathcal P(C)=\operatorname{Fun}(C^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$ be the Yoneda functor $c\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_C(-,c)$, where $\mathcal S$ is the infinity category of small spaces. For each $r_\alpha$ let $s_\alpha:\operatorname{colim}_{K_\alpha}yF_\alpha\to y(x_\alpha)$ be the map induced by its cocone. One may take $P_R(C)$ to be the full subcategory of $\mathcal P(C)$ on objects $X$ for which every $\operatorname{Map}(s_\alpha,X)$ is an equivalence, with $j_R=Ly$, where $L$ is the left adjoint to this inclusion. Colimits throughout are only the original $\mathcal U$-small colimits, even in the large-data case.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.6.2 and Remark 5.3.6.3, printed pp. 412-414; Proposition 5.3.6.11 and its proof, pp. 416-417 (finite-variable form); Remark 5.5.3.7 and Proposition 5.5.4.15, pp. 468 and 482 (small-data localization is presentable). Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks Project tag states this quasicategorical theorem.

proof.text: Keep $\mathcal U$ fixed and let $\mathcal K$ be its collection of small simplicial shapes. Choose a larger universe $\mathcal V$ in which $C$, $R$ and $\mathcal K$ are small, and form $A=\mathcal P_{\mathcal V}(C)$ with Yoneda functor $y$. This presheaf category is presentable by [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-presentability] (with $\mathcal V$ in place of its smaller universe) and admits all $\mathcal V$-small colimits. For each specified cocone form $s_\alpha:\operatorname{colim}yF_\alpha\to yx_\alpha$. The collection $S=\{s_\alpha\}$ is $\mathcal V$-small. By [lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints] its local objects form a presentable full subcategory $Q\subset A$ with a reflector $L:A\to Q$; colimits in $Q$ are $L$ of colimits in $A$. Use a replete model throughout.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.6.2, proof, first paragraph, p. 413; Proposition 5.5.4.15, p. 482

proof.text: Define $P\subset Q$ to be the intersection of all replete full subcategories containing every $Ly(c)$ and closed under $\mathcal K$-indexed colimits computed in $Q$. This is an actual full-subcategory construction. It has all $\mathcal U$-small colimits, computed in $Q$, because every subcategory in the intersection contains the colimit of any such diagram in the intersection. Put $j_R=Ly:C\to P$. By [lem-coef-infinity-small-localization-saturation], $Ls_\alpha$ is an equivalence. Applying $L$ to the colimiting cocone defining the source of $s_\alpha$ and then composing with $Ls_\alpha$ shows that $j_Rr_\alpha$ is colimiting. All its objects lie in $P$, so fullness gives the same universal mapping spaces in $P$. This also handles $K_\alpha=\varnothing$. Let $E=L^{-1}P\subset A$. It contains $y(C)$ and is closed under $\mathcal U$-small colimits. The adjunction restricts to $L_E:E\rightleftarrows P:i_E$, with $L_Ei_E\simeq1$.

For the target $Z$, choose yet another universe $\mathcal W$ with $\mathcal V\in\mathcal W$ containing its simplices and mapping spaces, so that every $\mathcal V$-small diagram is $\mathcal W$-small. The opposite Yoneda embedding $e:Z\to\widehat Z=\operatorname{Fun}(Z,\mathcal S_{\mathcal W})^{\mathrm{op}}$ is fully faithful, preserves all existing $\mathcal V$-small colimits and reflects them: apply the Yoneda and mapping-space limit criteria of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] to $Z^{\mathrm{op}}$. The target $\widehat Z$ admits all $\mathcal V$-small colimits, as these are pointwise limits of $\mathcal W$-spaces before taking the opposite. Replace the image of $e$ by its replete full essential image, using [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image]. It is closed under $\mathcal U$-small colimits in $\widehat Z$, since $Z$ has those colimits and $e$ preserves them. No $\mathcal V$-small cocompleteness of $Z$ is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 5.3.5.7, p. 405, and target enlargement in Proposition 5.3.6.2, p. 413

proof.text: Given $h:C\to Z$ sending $R$ to colimits, use [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-free-cocompletion] in universe $\mathcal V$ to extend $eh$ to a $\mathcal V$-colimit-preserving $H:A\to\widehat Z$. For each $s_\alpha$ its image is exactly the comparison $\operatorname{colim}ehF_\alpha\to ehx_\alpha$, hence an equivalence by the hypothesis on $h$ and step 3. The class of arrows inverted by $H$ contains $S$, all equivalences, and is closed under two-out-of-three, retracts, pushouts and $\mathcal V$-small arrow colimits: $H$ preserves the latter colimits, and pointwise equivalences are preserved by the colimit functor. By [lem-coef-infinity-small-localization-saturation] it therefore contains every localization unit $\eta_a:a\to iLa$. Consequently $H\eta$ is a natural equivalence.

Set $\widetilde H=Hi:Q\to\widehat Z$, so $H\simeq\widetilde HL$ via $H\eta$. It preserves $\mathcal V$-small colimits. Indeed a diagram $q$ in $Q$ has colimit $L\operatorname{colim}iq$; applying $\widetilde H$ gives $H(iL\operatorname{colim}iq)\simeq H(\operatorname{colim}iq)\simeq\operatorname{colim}Hiq$. This is the comparison on the specified cocone, by naturality of $H\eta$. Since $\widetilde HL y\simeq eh$, the inverse image under $\widetilde H|_P$ of the replete image $eZ$ contains $j_R(C)$ and is closed under $\mathcal U$-small colimits by step 3. The defining minimality of $P$ makes it all of $P$. Thus $\widetilde H|_P$ factors through $e$, giving a $\mathcal U$-colimit-preserving $\bar h:P\to Z$ and $\bar h j_R\simeq h$. This proves essential surjectivity.

We check full faithfulness, including transformation spaces. For any $\mathcal U$-colimit-preserving $f:P\to Z$, put $G=efL_E:E\to\widehat Z$ and extend $efj_R$ to $H_f:A\to\widehat Z$ by [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-free-cocompletion]. By [lem-coef-infinity-intermediate-presheaf-kan] the identity on $efj_R$ extends to $\alpha:H_f|_E\to G$, naturally in $f$. Step 4 applies to $H_f$ since $fj_R$ sends $R$ to colimits. Thus $H_f|_E$, $G$, and $\alpha$ descend across $L_E$ to $\beta:\widetilde H_f|_P\to ef$. Here descent is explicit: for any functor $B:E\to\widehat Z$ inverting every $\eta_a$, the functor $Bi_E$ has $Bi_EL_E\simeq B$ through $B\eta$; on transformations this same natural equivalence gives the inverse to precomposition with $L_E$. The restriction $\beta j_R$ is an equivalence. Its equivalence locus is closed under $\mathcal U$-small colimits, because both functors preserve them, and contains $j_R(C)$. Minimality of $P$ and the pointwise equivalence criterion give that $\beta$ and $\alpha$ are equivalences.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.6.2, proof, comparison transformation and its equivalence locus, p. 414

proof.text: For $f,g:P\to Z$ preserving $\mathcal U$-small colimits, the preceding descent identifies $\operatorname{Map}(ef,eg)$ with $\operatorname{Map}(efL_E,egL_E)$. Replace the first functor by $H_f|_E$ using step 6 and apply [lem-coef-infinity-intermediate-presheaf-kan]; the result is $\operatorname{Map}(efj_R,egj_R)$. The inclusion of $Z$ into $\widehat Z$ is fully faithful, including on coherent diagram mapping spaces, because it is the equivalence to a full essential image from step 3. Hence this is precisely $\operatorname{Map}(fj_R,gj_R)$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(C,Z)$. All maps here are restriction, identified using the identity on generators, so this proves the full faithfulness of the claimed restriction functor. Together with step 5 and [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image] it is the required equivalence of full infinity categories.

For later iteration record that pointwise $\mathcal U$-small colimits of colimit-preserving functors $P\to Z$ again preserve $\mathcal U$-small colimits. The pointwise rule is [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], applied in an ambient universe containing the indexing simplicial set $P$; only the colimits actually under consideration are needed. The interchange comparison $\operatorname{colim}_a\operatorname{colim}_bT(a,b)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_b\operatorname{colim}_aT(a,b)$ follows directly by mapping into $z$: both sides classify the same families of maps $T(a,b)\to z$ coherent in both indices, or equivalently the same iterated limit of mapping spaces with the two orders interchanged. This argument retains all simplices of those spaces. Thus the full category $\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{colim}}(P,Z)$ admits $\mathcal U$-small colimits computed pointwise. The identical interchange argument shows that $\operatorname{Fun}_R(C,Z)$ is closed under pointwise small colimits.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.6.11, proof by functor categories, pp. 416-417; pointwise colimit calculation

proof.text: Prove the finite-variable statement by induction on the number $n$ of variables. At $n=0$ the product is the terminal category, its functors to $Z$ are just $Z$, and the restriction is the identity. At $n=1$ use steps 1-7. Suppose it is known for $n-1$. The unary equivalence for $(C_n,R_n)$ identifies $D^{\prime\prime}=\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{colim}}(P_n,Z)$ with $D^\prime=\operatorname{Fun}_{R_n}(C_n,Z)$, both cocomplete by step 8, and preserves their pointwise small colimits. A coherent functor of $n$ variables is the same as a functor of the first $n-1$ variables into the coherent functor category in the last variable: degreewise this is the exponential identity $Z^{A\times B}=(Z^B)^A$. Preservation of a colimit in one of the first variables is pointwise in the last variable, by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. Apply the inductive equivalence with target $D^{\prime\prime}$ and then the displayed equivalence $D^{\prime\prime}\simeq D^\prime$. This gives exactly the two full categories in the $n$-variable assertion. All mapping spaces and higher transformations are retained because each operation is a functor-category restriction or an equivalence.

The restriction functors commute with postcomposition by any small-colimit-preserving functor of targets, and with restriction along any of the individual $j_{R_i}$: both composites are precomposition with the same product functor. These equalities of coherent functors provide the required compatibility, rather than independent choices of extensions. Full faithfulness in steps 7 and 9 identifies mapping spaces of transformations. Taking the cores gives the equivalence spaces, and applying the same mapping-space equivalence to parameter simplices gives all their compatibility homotopies. Inverses to the equivalences inherit these compatibilities with contractible ambiguity. Naturality in $Z$ is understood on cocomplete targets and colimit-preserving functors, since general target functors need not preserve the displayed full subcategories. No larger colimits have been added to the meaning of $\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{colim}}$.

Finally suppose $C$ and $R$ are $\mathcal U$-small. Repeat step 1 in $\mathcal U$ itself. By [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-presentability] $A=\mathcal P_{\mathcal U}(C)$ is presentable, and [lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints] says that its $S$-local subcategory $Q$ is presentable with reflector $L$. Every object of $A$ is a $\mathcal U$-small colimit of representables by [lem-coef-space-yoneda-density]. Applying $L$, every object of $Q$ is therefore a $\mathcal U$-small colimit of $Ly(C)$, since $Li\simeq1_Q$. Thus the closure $P$ of step 2 is all of $Q$. The construction is exactly the full subcategory and $j_R=Ly$ in the final paragraph of the statement, proving its presentability relative to the original universe. Empty $C$ gives the terminal category of presheaves and its initial generator-free cocompletion; a relation forcing an initial object is handled by the same map $s_\alpha$ with initial source.
